question: The Development Fund for MFI's is managed by the ___________.

options.text: Ministry of Finance, Govt of India

solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Reserve Bank of India**

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India was established in April 1935__.
 
• The RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India controls the issue and supply of the Indian rupee.
 
• It is basically the regulator of the Banking system in India. It strategizes monetary policy in India to control Inflation and money supply.
 
• The primary functions of the RBI include-
 __
 
• Formulates, implements and monitors the monetary policy
 
• Regulator and supervisor of the financial system
 
• Manager of Foreign Exchange
 
• Issuer of currency
 
• Regulator and Supervisor of Payment and Settlement Systems
 
 
 
• Sir Osborne A Smith was the first governor of the Reserve Bank of India.
 
• He held the post of governor from 1 April 1935 to 30 June 1937.
 
• Shri Shaktikanta Das is the present Governor of the RBI.
 
• He assumed charge as the 25th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India effective from December 12, 2018.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** State Bank of India​**

 
 
• The State Bank of India is formed by the merger or amalgamation of three banks namely 
 
 
• Bank of Bengal which was established in the year 1806
 
• Bank of Bombay incorporated in 1840
 
• Bank of Madras incorporated in 1843
 
 
 
• In 1921 all these three banks were amalgamated and came to be known as Imperial Bank of India.
 
• In the year 1955 the Reserve Bank of India acquired the controlling interest over the Imperial Bank of India and nationalized it and renamed it to State Bank of India. This is how the SBI was established.
 
 
 
• ​NABARD
 
 
• National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) is an apex development financial institution in India.
 
• It was established on 12th July 1982 by a special act of the parliament.
 
• NABARD's main focus is to uplift rural India by increasing the credit flow for the elevation of agriculture and rural non-farm sectors.
 
• It is responsible for the development of the small industries, cottage industries, and any other such village or rural projects.
 
• NABARD also maintains and oversees the rural financial institutions and ensures their smooth functioning.
